Feb. 27, 1847: John D. Nicoll sub-leases Franklin Wilson, for $2 and $7 a year, a lot on the east side of the lane between the Biays and Gilmor lands, the back end of Mumma's 1846 lot; the rent is redeemable at $116.67 (A.W.B. 378/206)

Feb. 14, 1917: Jacob H. Aull sells John T. Spellman Jr. and Helen P. Spellman the leasehold of 3026, the 15-foot house at the north-west corner of Greenmount Avenue and Vineyard Lane (formerly Gilmor Lane), subject to $72 a year; a $1,430 building-association mortgage the same day (S.C.L. 3109/316)

Oct. 1, 1903: Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens lease Joseph J. Willis the 3017 lot, 19 ft 2 in on the turnpike between the Aull lot and Rahe's, for 99 years renewable at $54 a year: the lease the $54 rent comes from (R.O. 2037/211)

Oct. 5, 1903: Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens sell Mary K. Fink, for $1,733, the $54 ground rent and reversion of 3017 and a second lot in fee on the turnpike: the start of the 3017 ground-rent chain (R.O. 2037/213)

Dec. 21, 1946: Mary C. Lehmann, widow, sells Harry R. and Alice M. Sinclair four ground rents, one of them the $54 rent on 3017 (typed 'No. 3013 Greenmount Avenue'); her title is Leopold Lehmann's will and Mary K. Fink's 1907 deed to him (M.L.P. 7060/156)

Oct. 12, 1972: Hyman B. Rubenstein, personal representative of Delmond F. Shields (d. May 2, 1971), deeds the 3032 leasehold ($66 rent) to People's Free Medical Clinic; Shields had it from Alva M. Shields in 1960 (R.H.B. 3152/289)

Mar. 2, 1868: George C. H. Coffield SUB-leases George Vandyke Smith the 79 ft lot (3113 to 3117) for the rest of his term less one year, at $150 a year, renewable, with a one-time buyout at $2,500 after ten years: the $150 rent is a sub-rent (E.H.A. 59/86)

Feb. 23, 1933: Hennegan and Lochboehler, trustees under a decree in Erhard Eyring et al. v. Miller Brothers Furniture Co., deed The Eyring Realty Corporation the 3117 leasehold for $19,000, subject to the $1,200 sub-rent (S.C.L. 5349/127, not /727)

Oct. 28, 1936: Safe Deposit and Trust Co., trustee under Ellen M. Schaeffer's will, sells Florence Crittenton Mission the $150 rent and reversion of the 79 ft lot (3113 to 3117, 3100-3102 Old York Road) for $4,137.93; Schaeffer had it from Henry Bradley in 1908 (S.C.L. 5669/442)

Dec. 30, 1936: Dorothy and Wilhelmina Dietrich and Helen Dietrich Butler deed Eyring Realty the $1,200 sub-rent of 3117, merging it; the 1928 Miller Brothers sub-lease is S.C.L. 4854/321 (Mar. 3, 1928), by Lula S. Dietrich, widow (S.C.L. 5686/215)

May 3, 1948: The Eyring Realty Corporation deeds Eyring Realty Enterprises, Inc. all its Baltimore City and County real estate, fee and leasehold, under a plan of reorganization; the deed names no lot (M.L.P. 7523/422)

June 1, 1966: the Wurtzburger trustees and Maryland National Bank sell 3200-3202 Greenmount to Harry B. Gorfine, surviving trustee of the two 1948 Katz trusts, for $35,500, half to each trust; it recites the whole Wurtzburger tenure from 'Elizabeth Ruth Samstag' (1936) (J.F.C. 2079/102)

July 5, 1972: Harry B. Gorfine resigns as trustee of the two 1948 Katz trusts (for Alan R. Katz and Barbara K. Gerstley) and names Arthur H. Katz his successor, Morris Fiddle second; co-trustee Joseph Smelkinson had died (R.H.B. 2927/593 and /596)

Mar. 6, 1872: Elizabeth D. Huff assigns James E. Sinclair, for $2,500, a leasehold of part of the tract 'Huntington' at the fork of the York Turnpike and Merryman's Lane, 10 perches on the road, which Andrew Brown assigned her in 1856: the first tract name for the 3200 block (E.H.A. 74/321)

Mar. 6, 1872: Elizabeth D. Huff assigns James E. Sinclair, for $2,500, a leasehold of part of 'Huntington' at the fork of the York Turnpike and Merryman's Lane, 10 perches on the road: very probably the 3200 apex and the frontage north of it (E.H.A. 74/321)

Oct. 24, 1873: Thomas J. and Henry R. Wilson, trustees under James Wilson's will, deed James E. Sinclair the reversion of the lot they leased him on Oct. 1, 1872 (E.H.A. 77/361), for $800: 44 1/2 ft on the turnpike north of 'Brown's lot' at Merryman's Lane (J.B. 84/387)

Apr. 9, 1866: Andrew Brown assigns Elizabeth D. Huff 'Brown's lot', the Huntington leasehold at the fork south of the 3224 ground, for $1,900, at one cent a year, from John Litzinger (1834) (J.H.L. 48/236)

Oct. 27, 1908: Henry and Carrie Bradley sell Ellen M. Schaeffer the $150 rent and reversion of the 79 ft lot 'immediately to the south of No. 4 Baltimore City Engine House'; Bradley had bought it three days before from Edward S. Peirce, trustee (S.C.L. 2459/514)

May 25, 1960: Alva M. Shields deeds the 3032 leasehold to Delmond F. Shields, 'a single person', for love and affection and his 'loving and devoted care and support ... for many years'; she had it from Allan Eli Cohan in 1930 (J.F.C. 873/14)

May 17, 1834: John Litzinger assigns Andrew Brown 'Brown's lot', the Huntington leasehold at the fork south of the 3224 ground, for $500; from the administrators of Frederick Parks, 1831 (T.K. 237/457)

June 3, 1887: John H. Stump assigns Mary Louisa and William Edward Peirce the $150 sub-rent and sub-reversion of the 79 ft lot (3113 to 3117) under Coffield's 1868 sub-lease, 'the original rent being one cent'; Stump had it from Mary J. Stump in 1886 (J.W.S. 160/431)

Feb. 18, 1901: Mary Louisa Peirce, 'about to be married', conveys all her property to Edward S. Peirce in trust for her life, then her children: the Peirce trust that sold the 3117 rent to Henry Bradley in 1908 (R.O. 1888/54)

June 30, 1930: Alva M. Shields, widow of Charles D. Shields, passes the 3032 leasehold through Allan Eli Cohan and back, taking a life estate with full power of sale, remainder to Delmond F. and Charles R. Shields; the Shieldses bought from Aull on Nov. 6, 1918 (S.C.L. 3281/596) (S.C.L. 5137/195)

Feb. 4, 1802: James Biays puts his three Ensor's Inspection lots (Spear's 9 7/8 acres from the Huntington red oak, Walker's 3 3/8 and Maidwell's 2 1/4) in trust with William Jackson, Levin Jones and John Smith for his wife Sarah for life, then their children: the trust the 2958 ground was sold out of in 1847 (W.G. 72/319)

May 10, 1803: John Gosuch (son of Thomas) conveys 'Harkin's Rest', 3 acres of Ensor's Inspection on the west side of the old main road at a stone marked I.H. 1765, to the Biays trustees for $1,200, on the same trusts for Sarah Biays and her children (W.G. 76/243)

Sept. 26, 1800: the end of James Maidwell's deed to James Biays of 'the aforesaid moiety of land' (the 2 1/4 acres with the orchard), $450, with Temperance Maidwell's release of dower; the deed begins on folio 62 (W.G. 67/63)

Apr. 16, 1874: William Thomas Wilson leases Margaret Hamilton, wife of Charles Hamilton, 100 ft on the west side of the turnpike just south of A. G. Mott's lot, 282 ft deep, at $325 a year, renewable, with a five-year buyout at $4,642.86 and a ban on saloons and nuisance trades; it is NOT the Eleanor Cross lease of the same date that the Keelty deed bounds on (J.B. 86/487)

Nov. 11, 1896: Francis E. and Florence E. Yewell deed John W. S. Brady, surviving trustee under Samuel Brady's will, the south-east half of the bed of Gilmor's Lane from 29th (formerly Holmes) Street to the Brady land's north-east line, in trust under the will's twelfth clause (R.O. 1647/561)

Feb. 24, 1906: the Brady estate trustees (Richard H. Woollen, Howard P. Sadtler, S. Procter Brady) and the Peabody Heights Company exchange lots along the old south-east side of Gilmor Lane between Calvert Street and Guilford Avenue, 27th to 29th Streets, to square the line to the city blocks (R.O. 2212/510)

Nov. 1, 1960: J. Paul and Carlyn L. Rocklin and Arthur L. Rocklin sell Chambers R. and Lucille R. Coffey 2936 Greenmount in fee, 14 ft at 248 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street; the Rocklins merged the ground rent in 1953 (J.F.C. 968/290)

Jan. 17, 1966: Ann B. Lyons sells Robert and Marjorie F. Orman 2934 Greenmount in fee, 14 ft at 234 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street, using the power of sale in her 1953 life estate from G. Agatha Riordan (J.F.C. 2017/404)

Research note: 2934 (234 ft 9 1/2 in), 2936 (248 ft 9 1/2 in) and 2958 (402 ft 9 1/2 in north of 29th Street) sit on one run of 14-ft lots measured from the same corner: 2934 to 2958 is thirteen houses on one survey, not just the eight of 2944 to 2958

Mar. 29, 1927: Richard (of Douglas, Wyoming), Martha and Mary L. Swormstedt deed Robert N. July 14, 1937: Rose I. Harding, widow, of Northumberland County, Virginia, sells the Wolfes the reversion and $54 rent of their Vineyard Lane lot, merging it; the rent came from Mary Clemens's Apr. 17, 1902 lease to Allen K. Wood, and the reversion from James B. Guyton (1910) (S.C.L. 5742/413)

June 18, 1954: Straw Man, Inc. assigns Harry W. and Bertha J. Hoover the leasehold of 3014 Vineyard Lane under a lease from Levi A. and Helen A. Barnett to Straw Man of the same day, 99 years renewable at $90; a $4,500 purchase-money mortgage follows (M.L.P. 9509/244)

Jan. 19, 1959: Marjorie C. Gamble, the straw, deeds 3014 Vineyard Lane back to Harry W. Hoover for life with full power to sell, lease and mortgage, remainder to his daughter Roma Vernelle Hoover; 'Title not examined' (J.F.C. 551/90)

Apr. 18, 1898: Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens lease Jacob H. Aull the 3011 tip lot (58 ft 4 in on the turnpike, 204 ft 7 in south of the two-mile stone) for 99 years renewable at $75 a year; the deed above it, to Lulie H. Wallace, sold the reversion (R.O. 1730/92)

Apr. 1, 1907: William Hall Wallace, bachelor, deeds Lulie H. Wallace, for $1 and love and affection, the 3011 reversion and its $75 rent under the 1898 Aull lease, which she had deeded him on Aug. 11, 1898 (R.O. 1748/566) (R.O. 2320/441)

Apr. 15, 1930: James M. and Ena M. Sinclair mortgage 3011 and 3013 Greenmount, in fee, to the Waverly Building Association of Baltimore County for a $1,040 advance on eight shares; Lennox B. Clemens is attorney and notary (S.C.L. 5109/220)

Apr. 7, 1934: the Sinclairs mortgage four lots (202 Homewood Terrace, 3011, 3013 and a one-cent leasehold on the Old York Road side by the Bateman-Provident line) to the Waverly Building Association for $1,913.29 (S.C.L. 5419/571)

Dec. 16, 1903: John P. Clark and James B. Kailer, executors of Francis P. Duggan, sell Richard and Barbara C. Swormstedt the $180 rent and reversion of 3010 for $3,000 (the rent at 6 percent); Mary Clemens had sold Duggan the rent on Oct. 31, 1901, the day she created it (R.O. 2050/46)

Apr. 17, 1902: Mary Clemens leases Allen K. Wood the Vineyard Lane lot behind 3010 for 99 years at $54, and the same day sells the rent and reversion to Mary L. Conway for $900 (the $54 at 6 percent) (R.O. 1952/245 and /247)

Apr. 18, 1898: Augustus D. Clemens Jr. and Mary Clemens sell Lulie H. Wallace the 3011 lot in fee, subject to the Aull lease of the same day, and 'especially the clear yearly rent of seventy five dollars', for $1,250 (the rent at 6 percent) (R.O. 1730/91)

Sept. 17, 1907: Mary K. Fink sells Leopold Lehmann the $54 rent and reversion of 3017 for $5 and other consideration; her title includes a deed from Estella Fink of July 31, 1907 (R.O. 2358/421) (R.O. 2369/13)

Apr. 16, 1874: William Thomas Wilson leases Elenor Cross, wife of John C. Cross, the 35 ft on the west side of the turnpike immediately south of Margaret Hamilton's 100 ft, 282 ft deep, at $113.75 a year, buyout $1,625 within five years: the Cross lease whose south line is the north line of Keelty's 1907 ground (J.B. 86/483)

Sept. 26, 1800: James Maidwell of Baltimore City sells James Biays, for $450 or £168 15s, 2 1/4 acres at the northern end of a tract of Ensor's Inspection adjoining Biays's land, east to 'the main road' and through the northern part of the orchard; no earlier title is recited (W.G. 67/62)

Sept. 14, 1953: Henry Lewis and Glen Marie Rosenthal sell the Rocklins the $75 rent and reversion of 2936, merging it; Earl Hoffmaster created the rent by a lease to Christina Caparrola on Mar. 7, 1944 and sold the Rosenthals the reversion the same day (M.L.P. 9274/275)

Nov. 9, 1953: G. Agatha Riordan, the straw, deeds 2934 back to Ann B. Lyons, widow, for life with full powers, remainder to Daniel J. Lyons; J. Milton Brandt witnesses and notarizes; no earlier title recited (M.L.P. 9327/460)

Research note, second look at the 1912 turnpike-company deed to Aull (S.C.L. 2727/29): its recital reads 'deed dated July 5, 187[ ] from David S. Wilson et al. ... Liber E.H.A. No 70 folio 92': the company's title is at E.H.A. 70/92

Feb. 3, 1870: the opening of the Wilson trustees' deed to the turnpike company: the 'gate house lot' on the west side of the turnpike had been 'for sixty years or more' in the company's possession under claim of title, and Alexander Contee Magruder had conveyed ground to James Wilson on May 14, 1844 (T.K. 341/328) (E.H.A. 65/404)

June 13, 1950: Mercantile Trust Company of Baltimore, surviving trustee under Francis X. Hooper's will, sells John T. Jr. and Helen P. Spellman the $72 rent and reversion of 3026 for $1,200 (the rent at 6 percent) on their notice to redeem, merging it (M.L.P. 8123/414)

Dec. 7, 1917: Florence W. Hooper, widow, and the Hooper trustees (Mercantile Trust and Deposit Co. and William Jenkins) divide Francis X. Hooper's real estate; the four 1912 Aull rents on 3026, 3028, 3030 and 3032 go to the trustees' two-thirds (S.C.L. 3177/132)

Nov. 6, 1918: Jacob H. Aull sells Charles D. and Alva M. Shields the 3032 leasehold ($66 rent), the fourth lot of Alice M. Chapman's 1916 assignment back to him; the Shieldses take a York Road Building Association mortgage the same day (S.C.L. 3281/596)

Jan. 13, 1925: Charles E. and Lilly M. Morris sell Daisy E. Masbach the 3028 leasehold ($66 rent), which Lawrence W. Sanner and wife had sold them on June 22, 1921 (S.C.L. 3770/255); she borrows $3,510 the same day (S.C.L. 4324/204)

Mar. 14, 1951: Nicholas Interrante, widower, sells Robert F. Podlich 3030 in fee; the leasehold came from Helen M. Bordley (Sept. 30, 1943) and the 1912 reversion from Charles T. and Ella B. Leight (Jan. 7, 1944); Podlich at once leases it to Marie B. Pipitone at $90 (M.L.P. 8386/70 and /72)

May 15, 1869: George C. H. Coffield assigns William Hammel, for $600, the south part of the Coffield tract, 125 ft 6 in on the east side of the turnpike up to Smith's 1868 lot, at one cent a year: the ground of the Methodist church lot and the Bateman lot (3105 to 3111) (E.H.A. 62/390)

Aug. 31, 1872: William Hammel sub-leases the Methodist Episcopal trustees (Edward Mallalieu and others) the south end of his Coffield ground, 55 ft on the turnpike to the Old York Road, at $165 a year, for a church and parsonage: very probably the Waverly Methodist Episcopal Church lot (E.H.A. 77/296)

Apr. 17, 1901: Walter I. Dawkins, administrator of James S. Bateman and of Mary A. Bateman, sells Clara V. Bateman two lots: the Old York Road lot from John Litzinger's 1866 lease to John H. White ($250, $58 rent) and the 70 ft 6 in of Coffield-Hammel ground on the turnpike ($3,000) (R.O. 1896/419 and /421)

July 9, 1934: James M. and Ena M. Sinclair assign the Provident Savings Bank back the one-cent lot behind the bank (24 ft by 86 ft 6 in to the Old York Road, by the 8-ft alley of the 1904 Bateman-Provident line), which the bank had assigned Sinclair on Mar. 26, 1920 (S.C.L. 5455/522)

May 14, 1844: Magruder, trustee of Philip G. Biays, sells James Wilson 3 a 1 r 12 p of 'Huntington' on the north side of Gough's road (Gilmor Lane) at the York Turnpike: the ground behind the 1912 lot of 3026 to 3032 (T.K. 341/328)

Oct. 31, 1901: Mary Clemens and Augustus D. Clemens Jr. sell Francis P. Duggan, for $3,000, the 3010 lot in fee 'and particularly the aforesaid rent' of $180 under the Wood lease of the same day (R.O. 1928/238)

Mar. 14, 1811: Elisha E. Russell, master mariner, puts his two Huntington lots of the day before (from William Jackson and from James Biays, the second on 'a road leading to Joseph Merryman's') in trust with George I. Brown and William S. Hollins to secure $4,735 (W.G. 112/471)

Sept. 2, 1809: Dorothy Brown, executrix of Jesse Brown, assigns James Biays 2 15/16 acres of 'Huntington' between the centre of the York Turnpike and the west side of the Old York Road, under Gough and Job Merryman's 1798 lease, at £4 8s 1d a year: the fork ground Leitzinger bought in 1847 (W.G. 104/48)

Aug. 11, 1898: Lulie H. Wallace, widow, under an Orphans' Court order in the estate of William Hall Wallace, an infant, sells him the 3011 rent and reversion for $1,250: a guardian investing a minor's money (R.O. 1748/566)

Mar. 1, 1879: a grading and macadam survey at Waverly for Birckhead (Bouldin papers) draws the York Road, Merryman's Lane, Barclay Street, 13th Street and Waverly Avenue, and a block lettered 'Sinclair's Lot'
Mar. 1, 1879: 'Sinclair's Lot' by Merryman's Lane on a Waverly grading survey for Birckhead: James E. Sinclair's ground of 1872 and 1873 (probable)

Huntingdon Chapel was probably the old stone barn: Bouldin's 1844 plat for John Gibson shows an 'Old Stone Barn' about 43 by 26 ft behind the Gate House Lot, and his 1849 chapel plat draws a 'Church' 43 ft 3 in by 27 ft 3 in, turned the same way, on the same spot
Bouldin's Nov. 10, 1849 plat of the chapel lot at the Gate House Lot: the 'Church' drawn 43 ft 3 in by 27 ft 3 in, the size and place of the 'Old Stone Barn' on his 1844 plat

St. John's, Huntingdon, papers in the Bouldin envelope: a list of eight vestrymen (Samuel Wyman, John Gibson, Thomas R. Hart and others) folded with the June 1844 survey of 20,000 sq ft by the eastern gate post of the first toll gate

Huntington resurveyed for John and Achsah Carnan, Sept. 29, 1757, 475 acres, patented Sept. 29, 1761: an 1810 certified copy of the certificate (recorded B.C. & G.S. 14/295; the patent is 15/219) in the Bouldin papers
The tract behind the 3200 fork: Huntington, the Carnans' 475-acre resurvey of 1757 (patent 1761), with Gay's plat, in an 1810 certified copy of the certificate (B.C. & G.S. 14/295)
Huntington Resurveyed: the Carnans' 1757 resurvey (475 acres), whose first tree is also a Merryman's Lot tree; patent Sept. 29, 1761; an 1810 certified copy of the certificate (B.C. & G.S. 14/295)

Feb. 3, 1781: Job Garretson to William Spear, 46 acres of Ensor's Inspection from a Huntington boundary tree (abstract in the Bouldin papers): probably the root of the Spear daughters' 1801 sale to James Biays

Coloured plat of James Biays's whole holding at the York Turnpike (Bouldin papers, used in the 1840s): the 1799 to 1804 Ensor's Inspection purchases and the 1803 Gough lots on the two sides of the 2-perch road, Philip G. Biays's 3a 1r 12p, Thornburgh's lot, Merryman's Road and the Old York Road

Coloured plat of James Biays's whole holding at the York Turnpike (Bouldin papers, used in the 1840s): the 1799 to 1804 Ensor's Inspection purchases and the 1803 Gough lots on the two sides of the 2-perch road, Philip G. Biays's 3a 1r 12p, Thornburgh's lot, Merryman's Road and the Old York Road

Coloured plat of James Biays's whole holding at the York Turnpike (Bouldin papers, used in the 1840s): the 1799 to 1804 Ensor's Inspection purchases and the 1803 Gough lots on the two sides of the 2-perch road, Philip G. Biays's 3a 1r 12p, Thornburgh's lot, Merryman's Road and the Old York Road
Apr. 19, 1847: Bouldin's survey of the Leitzinger wedge between the turnpike and the old York Road: 'on this lot is a two Story Brick House', and the deed's illegible distance is 6 6/10 perches
Apr. 19, 1847: Bouldin's survey of the lot sold to James Wilson at the turnpike and the lane ('the Lane is 1 7/10 p wide to the Stone of David Mumma's Lot'), seven weeks before the deed
Apr. 19, 1847: Bouldin's notes put St. John's church lot, '208 feet square', on the east side of the turnpike beside the Leitzinger wedge and its two-story brick house
MSA C2843-15 (the Bouldin envelope) read page by page, all 132 pages: what it holds, which pages reach the corridor, and the leads it adds

Oct. 24, 1801: Philip N. and Mary Nicholas (John Spear's only surviving child, William Spear's granddaughter) release James Biays their undivided share of the 9 7/8 acres of Ensor's Inspection the Spear daughters sold him in May, for $20 (W.G. 72/226)

Mar. 20, 1805: Gough and Prudence lease John Neale 9 a 3 r 32 p of 'Huntingdon resurveyed' on 'a private road laid out by said Harry Dorsey Gough leading from the York Turnpike to the grounds of Hugh Thompson', 59 pounds 14 shillings a year, 99 years renewable, fee for 995 pounds (W.G. 84/302)

Mar. 20, 1805: Gough leases Huntington in lots along his private road from the York Turnpike to Hugh Thompson's (the toll-gate lane, probable): John Neale's 9 a 3 r 32 p beside Samuel Vincent's lot and the road to Rutter's Mill (W.G. 84/302)

Negative search: the 1907 City grantor index has no deed from Henry E. Cook to the Lyonses; Cook's December entries are Gordon Avenue lots, one recorded the same day in the same book (S.C.L. 2390/404), so the mortgage's Cook recital is probably a clerk's carry-over

Pencil working plat of Jacob Aull's 1848 lot east of the Old York Road (Survey Papers, 'York Road No. 5'): the deed's seven courses, the Old York Road front re-measured at 172 ft, a corner building, lots in feet and a new 40-ft street

David Mumma sold John W. Beall a 1 3/4-acre lot running the full width between the York Turnpike and the Old York Road, 'between the 2 and 3 mile stones', with Ludwig Herring's lot to the south (stone marked 'DM' and 'LH'; Survey Papers, 'York Road No. 4')

Three 'York Road' survey envelopes read page by page (CE71-281 to 283): their indexes list 'John Whitely to James Wilson', 'John Brown to John Whiteley', 'Abell's Waverly' and the Biays/Ensor's Inspection papers, but those items were not filmed; what was filmed is mostly Towson and Govans
